name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulations (EU) No 1308/2013, (EU) 2021/2115 and (EU) No 251/2014 as regards certain market rules and sectoral support measures in the wine sector and for aromatised wine products
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to change the rules for the wine sector. It proposes letting winemakers give up unused planting rights without a fine, and letting countries limit new vineyards where there is too much wine. It also wants clearer labels for lower-alcohol and alcohol-free wine, easier electronic labelling, and more support for wine tourism, promotion abroad and crisis measures such as grubbing up vines and distilling surplus wine.

- Winemakers can hand back unused planting rights without a fine; countries may cap new vineyards.
- Labels get common terms for low-alcohol and alcohol-free wine, plus electronic ingredient lists.
- More money for promotion, tourism and crisis measures; Parliament's position now goes to EU governments.
